somalia.content: UN Political Mission Closes in Somalia as Constitutional Dispute Remains Unresolved - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME NEWS UN Political Mission Closes in Somalia as Constitutional Dispute Remains Unresolved Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Sunday November 1, 2026 Mogadishu (HOL) — The United Nations ended its political mission in Somalia on Saturday, withdrawing from a role it had played for more than three decades in mediating disputes among the country’s leaders, even as the government and opposition remain at odds over constitutional changes and the timing of the next elections. The departure leaves Somalia without an agreed international mechanism to help resolve a dispute over whether President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and parliament can remain in office until 2027. The government says constitutional amendments provide a legal basis for the extended terms. Opposition leaders reject that interpretation. The United Nations Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia, known as UNTMIS, formally concluded its operations after a two-year transition intended to transfer its responsibilities to Somali institutions and other UN agencies. The closure marks the end of a succession of UN political missions that began in the early 1990s, following the collapse of Somalia’s central government. Over the years, those missions helped convene negotiations among rival leaders, facilitated agreements on power-sharing and supported efforts to resolve election disputes. Their involvement did not eliminate Somalia’s recurring political crises, but it provided a channel through which competing factions could negotiate, often with international assistance. No comparable mediation framework has been established to replace that role, according to Al Jazeera, leaving the government and opposition to seek a settlement through direct negotiations. The federal government maintains that constitutional amendments adopted under Mohamud’s administration allow the president and members of parliament to remain in office until 2027. Opposition groups dispute that position, arguing against extending the current leadership’s tenure. Mohamud has invited opposition figures to talks aimed at resolving the dispute, but major opposition groups have not confirmed whether they will participate. The mission’s closure followed a request by the Somali government in 2024 to end the UN’s direct political role in the country. Government officials had accused the organisation of interfering in domestic affairs and sought greater Somali responsibility for political and institutional matters. The transition gradually transferred the mission’s responsibilities to national institutions and other parts of the UN system. The withdrawal does not end the UN’s presence in Somalia. Its humanitarian and development agencies will continue operating, although their mandates do not include the political mediation previously undertaken by the mission. Neither the government nor the opposition has announced an agreed procedure for resolving the constitutional dispute, and no alternative mediator has been formally designated if direct negotiations fail. Major opposition groups have yet to confirm whether they will accept Mohamud’s invitation to talks on the constitutional dispute and election timetable. somalia.content: Somalia’s security transition faces major test as international support comes under pressure – People Daily x Search GO Search... ePaper Search GO News Politics Business Insights Advertisement Insights Somalia’s security transition faces major test as international support comes under pressure Sunday 01st November, 2026 06:43 PM | By Kenneth Mwenda Members of Somalia-based Islamist insurgent group Al Shabaab. PHOTO/@DalsanTv/X Somalia’s efforts to take full responsibility for its security are facing a major test as the country navigates a changing international military presence, political divisions and persistent attacks by Al-Shabaab. The closure of the United Nations Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) on October 31, 2026, and Uganda’s announcement that it has started withdrawing troops after 20 years in the country have brought renewed attention to the challenges facing the security transition. The developments come as questions persist over the financing and logistical support of the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), which continues to support Somali forces in the fight against Al-Shabaab. A policy paper published by Balqiis Insights in July 2026 warned that Somalia could lose security gains if responsibility is transferred to national forces before the country has adequate financing, logistical support and political coordination. The report, titled No Time to Drift: Somalia and the Deadline for a Managed Security Transition , was written by Mustafa Osman and Samira Gaid. It argued that the transition required more than reducing the number of foreign troops or transferring responsibilities to Somali institutions. The authors warned that the country needed a clear plan to sustain military operations and ensure that Somali forces could hold territory reclaimed from Al-Shabaab. “A rapid loss of UNSOS support does not automatically translate to Somali self-reliance,” the paper stated. The warning comes at a time when Somalia is expected to assume greater responsibility for its security while continuing to depend on international partners for military and logistical assistance. AUSSOM’s logistical challenge One of the biggest concerns highlighted in the report is the dependence of AUSSOM on the United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS). While UNTMIS was responsible for political engagement, governance support and reconciliation, UNSOS provides logistical and operational assistance to African Union troops. The closure of the political mission does not mean that the separate support office has also closed. UNSOS provides essential services, including fuel, food, water, medical care, casualty evacuation, transport, aviation support, communications and engineering services. These services allow AU troops to operate across Somalia and support national forces in military operations against Al-Shabaab. Somalia President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud.PHOTO/https://www.facebook.com/HassanSheikhMahmud The Balqiis Insights paper estimated the UNSOS budget for the 2025/2026 financial year at approximately $537.2 million (Ksh69.6 billion), compared with between $166.5 million and $190 million (Ksh21.6 billion and Ksh24.6 billion) for AUSSOM, using an indicative exchange rate of Ksh129.57 to the dollar. The difference highlights the scale of logistical support required to keep the AU mission operational. The report warned that without a replacement arrangement, AUSSOM could struggle to maintain its operational capacity, even if its mandate remains in place. The financing question became more pressing after the United States indicated in July that it would not support the continuation of the existing UN logistical arrangement beyond the current authorisation period. In September, Reuters reported that Washington had agreed to a 12-month wind-down of logistical support, with the process expected to begin in January 2027. The proposal would allow time for the arrangement to be phased out rather than ending all support immediately on December 31, 2026. However, the proposed wind-down leaves Somalia and its partners with the challenge of finding alternative financing and logistical arrangements to sustain AUSSOM. The Balqiis report identified the absence of an agreed replacement for UNSOS as one of the major gaps in the security transition. Political divisions complicate transition The report also raised concerns about the lack of agreement among Somalia’s political leaders on the country’s security priorities. Disagreements between the federal government and regional administrations have complicated efforts to coordinate security operations and build a common approach to the transfer of responsibilities. Political tensions have also been heightened by disagreements over constitutional changes, election timelines and the distribution of power between Mogadishu and regional states. These divisions could affect intelligence sharing, military planning and cooperation between different security institutions. The closure of UNTMIS also removes a political mission that had supported dialogue, reconciliation and engagement between Somali leaders. The UN has maintained that its broader presence in Somalia will continue through its agencies, funds and programmes. However, humanitarian and development assistance does not automatically replace the political coordination and mediation functions previously carried out by UNTMIS. At the ceremony marking the end of the mission, Raisedon Zenenga, the UN Secretary-General’s Deputy Special Representative for Somalia, acknowledged the progress made but warned that significant challenges remained. “However, continued engagement by the international community will remain important to sustaining progress and addressing outstanding priorities,” Zenenga said. The African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) continues to assist Somali forces against Al-Shabaab, but concerns about its financing and logistical support have intensified. A report by Balqiis Insights warns that Somalia risks losing security gains if it assumes full responsibility without adequate resources and political coordination. The report highlights the critical role of the United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) for logistical support, which is now under threat as the U.S. plans to wind down its support. Additionally, political divisions among Somali leaders complicate the transition, hindering cooperation and intelligence sharing necessary for effective security operations. The UN emphasizes the need for ongoing international engagement to address these challenges and sustain progress in Somalia.

somalia.content: Somalia Gains Duty-Free Access to EU Market Under Trade Scheme - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME NEWS Somalia Gains Duty-Free Access to EU Market Under Trade Scheme Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Sunday November 1, 2026 Brussels (HOL) — Somali producers are eligible to sell qualifying goods in European Union markets without paying import duties or facing export-volume quotas, under a preferential trade arrangement that could help local businesses expand their overseas sales. The arrangement gives Somali exporters a potential cost advantage when competing in European markets, but businesses must still meet EU product standards and import requirements before their goods can enter the bloc. The EU Delegation to Somalia said in a social media statement that Somalia is among 33 African countries benefiting from the Everything But Arms (EBA) initiative, which provides duty-free and quota-free market access to countries classified among the world's least developed economies. The scheme covers eligible products except arms and ammunition, allowing qualifying shipments to enter EU markets without customs duties or restrictions on the quantity exported under the arrangement. For Somali businesses seeking customers abroad, the preferential terms remove two trade barriers that can make exporting more expensive or limit the volume of goods entering foreign markets. The EU Delegation said the arrangement has no fixed expiry date, offering businesses a continuing opportunity to develop export operations and seek customers in Europe. However, the announcement does not represent a newly negotiated trade agreement or an immediate increase in Somali exports. Somalia's access falls under an existing EU trade preference scheme. Export opportunities depend on meeting EU standards Although the arrangement removes tariffs and quotas, Somali producers must still comply with European quality standards and other import regulations. Those requirements remain a major consideration for businesses assessing whether they can sell their products competitively in the European market. Exporters that satisfy the standards could benefit from reduced trade costs and access to customers without the additional burden of EU import duties on qualifying goods. The absence of quotas also means eligible exporters would not face a fixed limit on shipment volumes under the scheme. The EU Delegation presented the arrangement as an opportunity for Somali businesses to expand production and strengthen their presence in international markets. However, any increase in exports would depend on businesses finding buyers, meeting regulatory requirements and developing the capacity to supply European markets. The delegation's statement did not identify particular Somali products expected to benefit, provide figures for existing exports to the EU or estimate how much additional trade the scheme could generate. It also did not announce any new export contracts or investments resulting from the preferential access. somalia.content: Somalia Opens Party Registration for 2027 Elections Amid Opposition Dispute - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME NEWS Somalia Opens Party Registration for 2027 Elections Amid Opposition Dispute Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Sunday November 1, 2026 Mogadishu (HOL) — Somalia has opened registration for political parties seeking to contest the country's planned 2027 federal elections, moving ahead with preparations for a one-person, one-vote system despite opposition demands for a political agreement on the electoral process. The registration window, which runs from November 1 to November 22, 2026, gives political groups three weeks to apply for participation in elections that would allow Somali voters to choose their parliamentary representatives directly under the commission's proposed framework. The National Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission announced the registration period as part of a timetable that schedules elections for both houses of the Federal Parliament on April 15, 2027, followed by a presidential election on May 15. The commission has also set November 22 as the deadline for submitting parliamentary candidate lists, requiring political groups to complete two major electoral preparations within the same period. Campaigning is scheduled to begin on February 27, 2027. The announcement marks a significant step in preparations for the planned federal elections, but it also brings the commission's timetable into sharper conflict with opposition groups that have rejected the process without a broader political settlement. Opposition challenges electoral framework Somali opposition groups have called for an agreement among political stakeholders before electoral preparations proceed, arguing that outstanding constitutional questions and disputes over the election framework must first be resolved. Their objections raise questions about whether the commission's timetable can secure wider political acceptance before parties begin campaigning. At the centre of the disagreement is the proposed one-person, one-vote system, which the commission intends to use for the federal elections. Under the plan, citizens would vote directly for their parliamentary representatives, replacing the approach to selecting lawmakers with the direct voting arrangements outlined by the commission. Opposition groups, however, maintain that the rules governing the elections and unresolved constitutional issues require political agreement before the process advances. The commission has continued its preparations despite those objections, maintaining the registration deadline and election dates already announced. No agreement resolving the opposition's concerns was identified in the information accompanying the registration announcement. advertisements November deadline puts political parties on the clock The immediate focus now shifts to political groups seeking to participate in the planned elections. They have until November 22 to complete registration, the same deadline established for submitting parliamentary candidate lists. The overlapping deadlines place pressure on parties preparing to enter the electoral process while disagreement continues over the framework under which they would compete. The commission's schedule leaves the period between the November registration deadline and the February 27 campaign launch for further preparations ahead of voting. Parliamentary elections are scheduled for April 15, with the presidential election planned for May 15, 2027. Whether those dates can proceed as planned remains closely tied to the unresolved dispute over electoral rules and constitutional questions. The next immediate test will come on November 22, when the registration and candidate-list deadlines expire, providing an early indication of which political groups are prepared to participate under the commission's proposed arrangements. The broader political question remains whether the commission and opposition stakeholders can reach an agreement before campaigning begins in February, or whether the dispute over the electoral framework will continue into the final months before the planned federal elections. somalia.content: Qatar Charity Concludes Campaign to Treat Heart Defects in Children in Somalia - Fana News Managers About Us Call Us العربية × Contact Us Womens Affairs Special Coverage Cultural Bulletin Health Reports Economic Reports Home ☰ English العربية العربية Call Us Contact Us Womens Affairs Special Coverage Cultural Bulletin Health Reports Economic Reports Home Home > Qatar Charity Concludes Campaign to Treat Heart Defects in Children in Somalia Home - Qatar Charity Concludes Campaign to Treat Heart Defects in Children in Somalia Political News ` Foreign Minister, Liberian Counterpart Discuss Bilateral Cooperation During Phone Call Foreign Ministry’s Undersecretary for Political Affairs Receives French Official More Economic News ` Workshop Held on Digital Guide Project for Cataloguing Government Services MSX Drops 53 Points More Cultural News ` Omani-Chinese Cultural Relations: A Deep Historical Legacy & Promising Prospects for Future Cooperation Oman Participates in Algiers International Book Fair 2026 More Sport News ` Oman Club Crowned Champions of Wings Handball Championship Second Round of Indoor Youth Handball League to Kick Off on 14 November More Special Coverage ` Jordan’s Q2 2026 GDP Expands 3.0%, Outperforming Regional Headwinds, International Forecasts ENV-KUWAIT-SUSTAINABLITYKuwait strengthens environmental sustainability through strategic initiativesBy Zahra Al-Kadhmi HLT-KUWAIT-SURGERYKuwait advances health sector with robotic, remote surgeryBy Mohammad Al-Moseb Saudi Arabia’s Voluntary Carbon Market Fuels the Shift to a Low-Carbon More Qatar Charity Concludes Campaign to Treat Heart Defects in Children in Somalia Mogadishu, November 01 (QNA) – Qatar Charity has concluded a campaign to treat heart defects in children, in cooperation with Somalia’s Ministry of Health, the Somali Sudanese Specialized Hospital and the Mogadishu Heart Center. Held under the “27th Night of Ramadan” initiative, part of the “Dafa’Al-Bala” campaign, it aimed to support and strengthen specialized healthcare services in Somalia. The closing ceremony was attended by HE Ambassador of the State of Qatar to the Federal Republic of Somalia Dr. Abdullah bin Salem Al Nuaimi. The campaign provided medical examinations and diagnostic assessments for 144 children with heart conditions and congenital heart defects. A total of 40 cardiac catheterization procedures were performed on children whose conditions required specialized treatment, under the supervision of a team of consultants and specialists in pediatric cardiology and cardiac catheterization. Speaking at the closing ceremony, Director of Qatar Charity’s Somalia Office Abdulfattah Adam Moallim said the campaign had exceeded its target of treating 35 cases by performing 40 cardiac catheterization procedures for children. This was a direct response to growing medical needs. He also announced that Qatar Charity is preparing to launch a specialized campaign for pediatric open-heart surgery before the end of the year. The campaign will address cases requiring advanced surgical interventions whose treatment needs could not be met through cardiac catheterization and heart defect repair campaigns. Partners and Doctors described the campaign’s success as a significant medical and humanitarian achievement, with Consultant in Pediatric Congenital Cardiology and Cardiac Catheterization at the Mogadishu Heart Center and Dean of the Faculty of Medicine and Surgery at Mogadishu University Dr. Mohamed Ahmed Mohamed affirming that the campaign’s results had given dozens of children a new chance at life and a more hopeful future. Consultant in Pediatric Cardiology and Cardiac Catheterization Dr. Iyad Al-Amouri praised the trust placed in the medical team by Somali families and the considerable efforts of young Somali medical professionals, whom he described as an important asset for the future of the country’s health sector. Qatar Charity previously carried out three specialized campaigns in Somalia to treat heart defects and conditions in children, benefiting 97 boys and girls. With the 40 cardiac catheterization procedures performed during the current campaign, the total number of children benefiting from therapeutic procedures and cardiac catheterization has risen to 137. By OMAR FARUK Associated Press November 1, 2026, 7:42 AM 1:24 FILE - Fishermen stand on the Indian Ocean beach at dusk in the former pirate village of Eyl, in Somalia's semiautonomous northeastern state of Puntland, Somalia, March 6, 2017. (AP Photo/Ben Curtis, File) The Associated Press MOGADISHU, Somalia -- MOGADISHU, Somalia (AP) — Somali pirates have seized an Iranian fishing vessel carrying 23 people, the Maritime Security Center Indian Ocean said, warning that the ship was approaching a commercial shipping lane and could become a floating base for further attacks. The Azini was hijacked Thursday between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said Sunday. The officer told The Associated Press that 12 pirates seized the vessel, which was carrying 21 Iranian crew members and two Somali security guards. He spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorized to speak with the media. The crew’s safety was unknown, the center said in an alert dated Saturday. In an updated warning, it said that pirates could use the vessel as a “mother ship” to support attacks on commercial vessels. The European Union’s naval Operation Atalanta was investigating. The center urged ships in the area to remain vigilant and report suspicious activity. The seizure follows a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean. By August, pirates had hijacked six commercial vessels since April , with some attacks taking place far from Somalia’s coastline. The captures included the oil products tanker Sibu 1, seized about 136 nautical miles (252 kilometers) east of al-Mukalla, Yemen. Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels against Saudi-linked shipping through Bab el-Mandeb have complicated routes used to move oil to world markets. Those disruptions have lengthened voyages and driven up tanker costs . The AP reported in September that some oil shipments diverted around Africa faced journeys up to a month longer, while daily spot charter rates for tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz had reached $1 million. International naval patrols and improved maritime security sharply reduced Somali piracy over the past decade. The latest seizures have renewed concerns about the threat to vessels off the country’s long coastline. Facebook Instagram X VKontakte Youtube Somali Guardian News Somalia Africa World Featured Editor Picks Editorials Home News Somalia Mawisley militias abandon front lines in central Somalia Mawisley militias abandon front lines in central Somalia November 1, 2026 Share Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – Hawadle clan militias that fought Al Shabaab alongside government forces have abandoned front-line positions in Somalia’s central Hiran region, Caasimada Online news website reported on Sunday, as clan leaders push to form an administration independent of the federal government. The fighters, known as Macawisley, have left posts in the Mataban and Buulo Barde districts, and there are fears they could also quit Jalalaqsi town. Clan fighters seized control of the regional capital, Beledweyne, over the weekend, taking over the provincial headquarters and other government offices. About 2,000 heavily armed clan fighters are now in the town as part of a plan by Hawadle political figures to create an authority separate from Mogadishu and from Hirshabelle, the federal member state that includes Hiran. Fears of further defections There are concerns that Hawadle soldiers serving in the federal army in Hiran could also defect, a move that would leave the remaining government-held areas exposed to Al Shabaab. The insurgent group has retaken much of the ground gained by the militias and the army in 2022 and 2023, after a major counter-offensive in 2025. The Macawisley were formed in 2022 to fight Al Shabaab and received support from the federal government, Ethiopia and the United States. Abdullahi Mohamed Ali Sanbalolshe, a former head of the National Intelligence and Security Agency, said recently that they planned to set up an administration to confront the government in Hiran. He said it would ally with anyone, including Al Shabaab, to remove President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. Dispute over Hirshabelle leadership Hawadle politicians say Mohamud promised their clan the Hirshabelle presidency, then reneged and sidelined them. They accuse the federal government of backing incumbent regional president Ali Gudlawe in a re-election vote that Mogadishu organised and whose outcome it controlled. It is unclear how the standoff will end or whether Mogadishu will send reinforcements to Hiran region. سريعا وحقق الفوز على منافسه "غاسوجي" الرواندي، عقب الخسارة الثقيلة التي تعرض لها في الجولة الماضية. وحققت إدارة النادي مكاسب مهمة قبل الاستحقاقات الحاسمة، بفضل خطط مدروسة شملت مواصلة تدعيم صفوف الفريق بمحترفين أجانب، والاستعداد لتلبية مطالب المدرب بشأن إحداث تغييرات جذرية في التشكيلة. وأسهمت هذه الخطوات في إشعال المنافسة بين اللاعبين، ما انعكس إيجابا على مستويات عدد من النجوم الذين استعادوا بريقهم بضرورة تطوير مستوياتهم وتقديم الأفضل لضمان مكانهم في التشكيلة. وظهرت نتائج هذه السياسة سريعا، بعدما توج صانع الألعاب عبد الرؤوف يعقوب بجائزة أفضل لاعب في المباراة الأخيرة. من جانبه، استعاد القائد محمد أفريقيا . كما استعاد المهاجم أداما كوليبالي مكانه في صفوف الفريق بتوقيت مثالي، قبل خوض المنافسات الأفريقية، ليمنح زينباور إضافة نوعية، باعتباره أحد الركائز الأساسية التي أسهمت في الطفرة التي حققها الهلال خلال السنوات الأخيرة. اقرأ أيضًا الهلال السوداني يستعيد توازنه بفوز ثمين في الدوري الرواندي زينباور يتحرك بعد السقوط المدوي.. قرارات حاسمة تهز الهلال وسارع زينباور إلى منح لاعبه المالي مزيدا من football.content: خلافات تهدد مشروع أبياه مع المنتخب السوداني.. والرحيل يلوح في الأفق — تاق برس اعجاب المتابعين الإثنين, نوفمبر 2, 2026 من نحن السياسة التحريرية للإعلان على تاق برس اتصل بنا تاق برس - اخبار السودان والعالم الرئيسية أخبار عاجلة سياسية منوعات وثقافة إقتصاد رياضة علوم وتكنلوجيا مقالات أخري تقارير صحة الرئيسية أخبار رياضة خلافات تهدد مشروع أبياه مع المنتخب السوداني.. والرحيل يلوح في الأفق خلافات تهدد مشروع أبياه مع المنتخب السوداني.. والرحيل يلوح في الأفق بواسطة editor في أكتوبر 31, 2026 193 مشاركة متابعات تاق برس – تتجه العلاقة بين الغاني كواسي أبياه، المدير الفني للمنتخب الوطني السوداني الأول، والاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم نحو منعطف بالغ الخطورة، في ظل تصاعد الضغوط والتدخلات التي باتت تحاصر المدرب، وتضع تجربته مع صقور الجديان على المحك، وسط مؤشرات متزايدة على اقتراب نهاية مشواره مع المنتخب. وتشير المعلومات التي تحصل عليها “الترا سودان” من داخل مجلس إدارة الاتحاد إلى أن أبياه بات يشعر بأن ما يتعرض له يمثل تحركات منظمة تستهدف تقويض صلاحياته وإضعاف موقفه، تمهيداً لإبعاده عن قيادة المنتخب. وهو ما أسرّ به لعدد من المقربين منه، معبّراً عن استيائه الشديد من الأجواء التي يعمل فيها. وبحسب المعلومات ذاتها، فإن المدرب الغاني بات يعتقد أن هناك مخططاً يُحاك ضده، وأن بعض القرارات والتوجهات الأخيرة داخل الاتحاد لا يمكن فصلها عن مساعٍ لإجباره على مغادرة موقعه، بعدما وجد نفسه في مواجهة تدخلات متكررة في صميم اختصاصاته الفنية. التغييرات التي طالت الجهازين الإداري والفني المساعد لم تكن أمراً عابراً بالنسبة للمدرب الغاني، خصوصاً بعد إبعاد المدير الإداري أبوبكر الماحي، وابتعاد المدرب العام صلاح الفنج عن موقعه ضمن المنظومة التي عملت معه خلال الفترة الماضية. ويمثل الرجلان عنصرين مهمين في منظومة أبياه، وكان المدرب ينظر إليهما باعتبارهما من ركائز الاستقرار داخل المنتخب، الأمر الذي دفعه إلى المطالبة بإعادة ترتيب الأوضاع بما يضمن عودة الانسجام إلى الجهازين الفني والإداري. لكن ما حدث عزز شعوره بأن هناك توجهاً لإعادة تشكيل المنظومة المحيطة به، دون اعتبار لرؤيته أو احتياجاته، وبكوادر لا تمتلك بالضرورة الخبرة المطلوبة للعمل في منتخب بحجم صقور الجديان. ومن أكثر الملفات التي أثارت غضب أبياه الضغوط المتواصلة بشأن إبعاد عدد من أصحاب الخبرة والعناصر الأساسية التي شكلت العمود الفقري للمنتخب خلال مشواره الأخير. فالمدرب الغاني لا يرى مبرراً للتخلي عن عناصر أثبتت جدارتها وقدمت الكثير للمنتخب، لمجرد ارتباط بعضها بملف المطالبة بالمستحقات المالية. كما لا يخفي تحفظاته على محاولات فرض أسماء جديدة ضمن القائمة، دون أن تكون هناك قناعة فنية مكتملة بشأن قدراتها. وتفاقمت الأزمة مع التوجه نحو تغيير نسبة من قوام المنتخب وإقحام عناصر من منتخب الشباب، في وقت يرى فيه أبياه أن الإحلال والتجديد لا ينبغي أن يتحولا إلى قرارات فوقية تتجاوز التقييم الفني واحتياجات المنتخب. ولم تتوقف مصادر الإحباط عند التدخل في اختيار اللاعبين وإدارة الجهاز الفني، بل امتدت إلى عدم تنفيذ عدد من البرامج الإعدادية التي اقترحها المدرب، وفي مقدمتها إقامة معسكر مبكر عقب فراغ الهلال والمريخ من مشاركتهما في البطولات الأفريقية. وكان أبياه يعوّل على الاستفادة من تلك الفترة في تجهيز المنتخب بصورة مثالية، والاستفادة من وجود العناصر الأساسية في السودان. غير أن عدم الاستجابة للمقترح أضاف حلقة جديدة إلى سلسلة الخلافات بينه والاتحاد. وبدا للمدرب أن برامجه وتصوراته لا تجد الاهتمام المطلوب، وأنه مطالب بتحقيق النتائج وتحمل المسؤولية كاملة، دون أن تتوفر له الظروف والصلاحيات اللازمة. التطور الأكثر إثارة في هذه الأزمة أن أبياه، وفقاً للمعلومات التي تحصلت عليها مصادرنا، لمح للمقربين منه بأن مواجهتي المنتخب أمام السنغال ذهاباً وإياباً قد تكونان آخر مشاويره مع صقور الجديان. وتشير هذه المعطيات إلى أن المدرب الغاني بدأ بالفعل التفكير في وضع حد لتجربته عقب المباراتين، في ظل قناعته بأن الأجواء الحالية لم تعد تساعده على مواصلة العمل بالصورة التي يريدها، وأن حجم التدخلات والضغوط تجاوز الحدود التي يمكن التعايش معها. وإذا مضى أبياه في هذا الاتجاه، فإن المنتخب الوطني سيكون أمام خسارة مدرب كبير قاده إلى مرحلة مميزة من النتائج والإنجازات، في وقت يحتاج فيه إلى الاستقرار والاستمرارية أكثر من حاجته إلى الدخول في مغامرة فنية وإدارية جديدة. ما يحدث الآن يتجاوز خلافاً حول قائمة أو لاعب أو معسكر إعدادي. نحن أمام أزمة ثقة تتسع يوماً بعد يوم، ومدرب بات يشعر بأنه مستهدف، وأن هناك من يعمل على إضعاف تجربته وإفقاده أدوات النجاح، قبل أن يصبح رحيله أمراً واقعاً. والسؤال الذي ينبغي أن يجيب عنه الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم ليس ما إذا كان أبياه سيغادر فحسب، بل من يتحمل مسؤولية الوصول بعلاقة المنتخب مع مدرب صنع معه إنجازات كبيرة إلى هذه المرحلة؟ هل هناك مشروع فني بديل يستحق التضحية بتجربة أبياه؟ أم أن صقور الجديان يدفعون ثمن صراعات وتدخلات إدارية لا علاقة لها بمصلحة المنتخب؟ المؤكد أن خسارة أبياه، إن حدثت بالطريقة التي تلوح في الأفق، ستكون بداية هدم مشروع كان يستحق الحماية والاستقرار والبناء عليه. اتحاد كرة القدم صقور الجديان كواسي أبياه 193 مشاركة أخبار ذات صلة رياضة أبياه يعلن القائمة الأولية لصقور
